IMPORTANT RAG GOVERNANCE
------------------------
1. Source priority for factual answers:
   P1 = current VR-controlled internal records/certificates/catalogue and current official vrcoatings.com pages.
   P2 = other current first-party VR materials such as social/company pages and current partner pages.
   P3 = older/legacy official VR website pages and historical internal marketing documents.
   P4 = third-party directories, corporate databases and search-indexed public records.
2. Never convert UNKNOWN / TBC, PROPOSED, INFERRED, or a CONFLICT record into a guaranteed VR specification.
3. Never publish a price unless a current VR commercial source explicitly confirms the exact model and price.
4. Never state product-to-accessory compatibility from proposed cross-references without engineering/commercial validation.
5. For product selection, ask for material/chemistry, viscosity, solids/abrasiveness, required pressure, delivery rate, temperature, mixing ratio if any, utilities, application method, environment/hazardous-area requirements and connection constraints.
6. When two sources conflict, prefer the higher-priority and newer first-party source, but disclose material conflicts where relevant.
7. Marketing metrics such as '30+ product lines', '100+ product lines', and the internal 143-product master use different counting schemes. Do not treat them as the same metric.
8. 'Founded/operating since 1985' and legal incorporation on 21 March 2003 are not inherently contradictory: the present private limited legal entity was incorporated in 2003 while VR's operating history is stated by first-party sources as beginning in 1985.

DATA STATUS VOCABULARY
----------------------
VR VERIFIED = supported by VR documentation.
EXTERNALLY VERIFIED = supported by an authoritative external source; not automatically a VR product specification.
DERIVED = calculated only from verified values.
INFERRED = engineering interpretation requiring review.
PROPOSED = recommended structure/content or compatibility candidate requiring approval.
UNKNOWN / TBC = cannot responsibly be determined from the current source set.
CONFLICT = multiple records disagree; do not silently choose unless a higher-priority current source resolves it.

SECTION 1 — CANONICAL COMPANY PROFILE
=====================================
Canonical name: V R Coatings Pvt. Ltd. / VR Coatings Pvt. Ltd.
Industry: industrial coating equipment, spray painting equipment, dispensing equipment, and fluid-handling machinery.
First-party operating-history statement: founded / operating since 1985 in Bhosari, Pune, India.
Core activities: design, manufacture, installation, sales, service and support of industrial spray-painting and fluid-handling equipment used for spraying, dispensing, pipe coating, transfer, metering, proportioning, mixing and dosing.
Core material classes handled across the portfolio include paint, sealant, adhesive, wax, oil/lubricants, grease, solvents, epoxy, polyurethane, polyurea, intumescent/passive-fire-protection coatings, waterproofing materials, hot-melt adhesives, varnish/lacquer, anti-corrosion coatings, zinc-rich primers, semi-solid pastes, isocyanate and polyol.
Business model: standard equipment plus customized / engineered-to-order systems for industrial applications.
Current official web positioning includes 40+ years experience, 15+ industries served, international certifications and Made-in-India manufacturing.
The current official homepage markets 100+ product lines; the current About page markets 30+ product lines; the controlled internal catalogue retains 143 product identities. These are different counting/marketing schemes and should not be reconciled without a defined taxonomy.
Current official website claim: 450+ dedicated employees. LinkedIn classifies company size as 201–500 employees. Treat 450+ as a current first-party marketing claim rather than an audited headcount.

SECTION 2 — HISTORY AND MILESTONES
==================================
1985 — Current official website and LinkedIn state VR Coatings was founded in Bhosari, Pune; the official About page says it began manufacturing airless spray painting equipment for Indian industries.
1990s — Official website history says the range expanded into two-component systems, transfer pumps and accessories, with early certifications.
1998 — An internal company-profile history says VR built its own Drum Press after the earlier supplier Kopper Schmidt closed; cylinders were made in steel and pumps machined from solid parts.
2003-03-21 — Government MCA registration list records V R COATINGS PRIVATE LIMITED, CIN U29299PN2003PTC017801, registered on this date.
2004 — Internal company profile states a Pune factory milestone.
2000s — Current official website history says CE and ATEX certification milestones enabled European-market / hazardous-area applications.
2010s — Current official website history highlights DRAGON PFP, POLYUREA spray system and electronic VRC-MIX range.
2013 — Internal company-profile Drum Press history records an upgrade: cylinders/pump modified, aluminium hoists, new control block, and dies/moulds for higher production quantities.
2018 — Internal company profile states a Wai factory milestone. ISO certificate records original ISO certification date 12/09/2018.
2019 — Internal company-profile Drum Press history mentions two-hand operation, IoT-ready control panels and 'Super Melt' for very high-viscosity materials.
2026 — Current first-party sources continue to state 'Since 1985' / 40+ years. LinkedIn also references the 41st Foundation Day in 2026.

HISTORY CONFLICT NOTE:
- One internal company-profile slide contains the wording '1987 Inception Of the Company' in the Drum Press history section, while current official corporate sources consistently state 1985. Use 1985 as the canonical company founding year. Treat the 1987 wording as a historical-document conflict or a possible product/distribution milestone unless VR management clarifies it.

Examples of application mapping used on the official website:

- Defence: vehicle/naval protective coatings and camouflage-type applications.
- Aerospace: coating of fuselage, wing and landing-gear components.
- Railways: bogie/coach zinc primer and topcoat applications.
- Oil & gas: pipelines, storage/refinery assets, internal/external pipe coating and tube varnish.
- Wood/furniture: PU, lacquer, varnish, sealer and stain.
- Waterproofing/insulation: polyurea, PU foam, floors, roofs and tunnels.
- General manufacturing: primer/topcoat, circulation, grease and lubrication.
- Wind energy: turbines, blades and towers.
- Agriculture/earthmovers: tractors, harvesters, excavators and related equipment.

SECTION 13 — MODEL / PRODUCT NOTATION AND INTERNAL ENGINEERING NOTES
==================================================================
Internal company profile explains pump model notation examples such as 28:550 as a 28 pressure-ratio pump delivering 550 cc per cycle. Do not generalize every model string without checking verified variant/technical data.
Internal profile states pumps can be provided with heaters for heated media up to 210°C; model/material compatibility must be confirmed.
Follower plate / seal material options shown in internal profile include NBR (nitrile), PU (polyurethane), EPDM, FKM/Viton and silicone, plus customized discs for non-standard drums.
Automatic dispenser examples shown internally: CCV 400 (up to 400 bar), VRIA (up to 250 bar) and robotic dispenser (up to 250 bar and up to 210°C). Verify current model specification before quotation.
Hand-held dispenser examples include EXT and HAWK in heated applications up to 210°C.
Booster pump examples include 48:720 and 38:910; the internal profile explains 38:910 as pressure ratio 38 and 910 cc/cycle.

Note- Add all the faqs under below categories and show it categorically in the website.

General
What does VR Coatings do?
 We manufacture and export dispensing machines, spray painting equipment, pumps, and fluid handling systems.
Where is VR Coatings based?
 Our HQ and plant are in Pune, India, with a German subsidiary (DOT) for global operations.
How long has VR Coatings been in business?
 We’ve been serving industries with innovative coating and dispensing solutions for over 30 years.
Which industries use your products?
 Automotive, railways, aerospace, heavy engineering, adhesives & sealants, electronics, pharma, and more.
Do you serve both large enterprises and small businesses?
 Yes, we work with OEMs, Tier-1s, SMEs, and specialized manufacturers.
Are your machines made in India?
 Yes, our machines are designed and manufactured in India with German collaboration.
Do you have international certifications?
 Yes, our systems comply with CE and other industry standards.
Do you have a German office?
 Yes, through DOT (Germany), ensuring fast support across Europe.
Do you attend exhibitions or trade shows?
 Yes, we regularly participate in global industrial summits and expos.
What makes VR Coatings unique?
 Customized engineering, robust after-sales support, and proven global trust.
Products & Solutions
What types of spray painting equipment do you offer?
 Airless systems, electrostatic spray guns, auto painting machines, and complete solutions.
Do you provide cartridge filling systems?
 Yes, we offer cartridge fillers for adhesives, sealants, and other materials.
What are your dispensing machines used for?
 For accurate metering, mixing, and dispensing of adhesives, sealants, and coatings.
What are transfer pumps used for?
 They handle viscous materials like sealants, paints, and adhesives with high efficiency.
Do you offer hydraulic dosing systems?
 Yes, we provide hydraulic and pneumatic dosers for precision applications.
Do you supply spares and consumables?
 Yes, we stock spares and consumables for long-term machine support.
Do you manufacture standard and customized machines?
 Yes, we offer both standard models and tailor-made solutions.
Can your machines handle high-viscosity materials?
 Yes, our pumps and dosers are built for high-viscosity adhesives and coatings.
Do you supply complete paint shop setups?
 Yes, we design and supply turnkey painting solutions.
Can your machines integrate with automation lines?
 Yes, our systems can be integrated into robotic and automated production lines.
Do you provide fluid handling solutions beyond coatings?
 Yes, we serve adhesives, sealants, resins, inks, and specialty chemicals.
Are your products energy-efficient?
 Yes, our machines are designed for high efficiency and reduced wastage.
Sales & Exports
Do you export internationally?
 Yes, to Europe, Asia, Middle East, Africa, and beyond.
Can I order directly from Germany?
 Yes, DOT Germany supports EU customers for faster delivery.
Do you work with OEMs?
 Yes, we supply directly to OEMs and Tier-1 companies.

 Yes, live or virtual demos are available.

 Fill out the inquiry form or email sales@vrcoatings.com.

 Yes, we manage bulk, custom, and repeat orders globally.

 Lead times vary by product but are communicated clearly at order.

 In some cases, yes—contact our sales team for details.

 We offer flexible terms depending on project size and client profile.

 Yes, we have partners in Europe, Asia, and other regions.

 Yes, we can ship as per your preferred Incoterms.

 Yes, we welcome customer visits to our Pune facility.

 Yes, our engineers handle installation and setup at your site.

 Yes, we train your staff to ensure smooth operation and safety.

SECTION 32 — EXCLUDED CONTAMINATION SOURCE
==========================================
The workbook contains a COMPETITOR BENCHMARK sheet (e.g., Graco, WIWA and other external manufacturers). It is intentionally NOT injected into this monolithic VR factual body because competitor specifications must never be retrieved as VR specifications. The catalogue itself states competitor values are permitted only for field-schema/selection-logic benchmarking.

SECTION 34 — DEPLOYMENT / RAG ANSWERING POLICY
=============================================
Recommended retrieval behavior for the chatbot:
- For 'Who is VR Coatings?' answer from Sections 1–8 first.
- For location/contact questions, use Section 4 first.
- For certifications, use Section 6 and exact certificate records; avoid generalizing certification to every product.
- For client questions, use Section 11 but phrase as 'listed in VR Coatings first-party client materials' unless a current relationship is explicitly documented.
- For product factual questions, retrieve Product Master + Variant Master + Technical Data for the same Product ID.
- For material/application suitability, retrieve Application Master + Material Master, but obey Data Status. INFERRED mappings require validation.
- For system/accessory compatibility, retrieve Cross-Reference / System Configuration / Accessory Matrix only as candidate guidance; engineering validation is mandatory.
- For spare part numbers, never invent. If part number is TBC, say it is not present in the controlled source and ask for exact product/model/serial/BOM.
- For prices, answer 'contact sales / price on application' unless a current VR-approved price list for the exact model is added to the KB.
- For unknown fields, surface the relevant TBC/Conflict record instead of extrapolating.
- When a user provides new application inputs, use the customer-selection questions to gather missing conditions before recommending a model.
- Cite exact model/variant and source status in high-stakes technical answers.
- Do not treat AI illustrative renders as technical drawings or dimensional evidence.
